tool.title: Hadronic processes at work in 5BZB J0630-2406
tool.excerpt: Hadronic processes at work in 5BZB J0630-2406. Recent observations are shedding light on the important role that active galactic nuclei (AGN) play in the production of high-energy neutrinos. In this study, we focus on one object, 5BZB J0630-2406, which is among the blazars recently proposed as associated with neutrino emission during the first 7-yr IceCube observations. Modelling the quasi-simultaneous, broad-band spectral energy distribution, we explore various scenarios from purely leptonic to lepto-hadronic models, testing the inclusion of external photon fields. This theoretical study provides a complementary testing ground for the proposed neutrino-blazar association. Despite being historically classified as a BL Lac, our study shows that 5BZB J0630-2406 belongs to the relatively rare sub-class of high-power flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs). Our results indicate that interactions between protons and external radiation fields can produce a neutrino flux that is within the reach of the IceCube detector. Furthermore, the spectral shape of the X-ray emission suggests the imprint of hadronic processes related to very energetic protons.

tool.excerpt: Far-right AfD scores record win in German state election-Xinhua Far-right AfD scores record win in German state election Source: Xinhua | 2026-09-07 02:19:30 | Editor: huaxia A voter arrives at a polling station in Magdeburg, Germany, Sept. 6, 2026. The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has won Sunday's state election in Saxony-Anhalt with a record 44.5 percent of the vote, according to an exit poll released by public broadcaster ARD. (Xinhua/Zhang Haofu) MAGDEBURG, Germany, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has won Sunday's state election in Saxony-Anhalt with a record 44.4 percent of the vote, according to an exit poll released by public broadcaster ARD. The Christian Democratic Union (CDU), led by incumbent state leader Sven Schulze, suffered a heavy blow, plunging to 18.4 percent, down from 37.1 percent in 2021, the poll showed. The Left party came in third with 9.3 percent, followed by the Greens with 8.7 percent and the Social Democratic Party (SPD) with 8.4 percent. The newly formed Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) hovered right on the 5-percent threshold to enter the state parliament, while the business-friendly Free Democratic Party (FDP) crashed out with just 2.2 percent. Conceding defeat, Schulze acknowledged the AfD's clear victory, while urging political leaders across Germany to heed the message sent by voters. In Berlin, head of the Chancellery Nina Warken called the election outcome a "watershed moment" for the CDU, describing it on broadcaster ZDF as a "very, very difficult result." Warken also insisted that the federal government would resolutely press ahead with its planned reform agenda. In the 83-seat state parliament, the AfD is projected to secure 39 seats, three seats shy of an absolute majority needed to govern alone. The AfD's 35-year-old state lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund hailed the result, declaring that "the people have sent a clear signal." Speaking to ARD, Siegmund also signaled a shift from his pre-election stance of only seeking office through an absolute majority, noting that his party is now open to a coalition. However, all other mainstream parties have repeatedly ruled out entering a coalition with the AfD. It remains unclear how a viable state government will be formed. ■ A voter arrives at a polling station in Magdeburg, Germany, Sept. 6, 2026. The far-right Alternative for Germany
